requirement:
Saved execution-coverage checks read the current coverage set under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.current` from SQLite. Each check
uses one coherent database snapshot of test identities, states, provenance,
and processed measurements, so a replacement or update cannot mix results
from different snapshots within the same check.

Checks do not search historical runs or use a separate report-selection
metadata cache. Current test identities, states, and provenance can be read
without loading their detailed measurements.

Only current results with complete, available measurements contribute to
coverage under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`.
Pending, running, and unavailable entries are reported under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`. Checking does not build
or execute tests and never restores a superseded attempt.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Each obligation maps to a marked test with real assertions.

- **One coherent snapshot per check.** `src/execution_coverage/store.rs#mod[tests]/fn[replacement_between_snapshot_queries_cannot_mix_configurations_or_results]` commits a replacement through a SQLite trace callback while the reader's snapshot is being read. It asserts that the first snapshot's configuration, latest run, test identity and measurements (7) all come from the old state. A later snapshot sees only the new state (9).
  - `metadata_queries_skip_measurements_and_snapshots_survive_subsequent_replacement` also shows that an already-taken snapshot survives a replacement.
  - A search for `.snapshot(` shows `load_saved` in `src/execution_coverage/book.rs` takes exactly one `snapshot(true)`. A saved check therefore does not split its reads across snapshots.
- **No historical search, and a superseded attempt is never restored.** `unreadable_history_cannot_reintroduce_an_older_success` in `book.rs` records an older success and a newer attempt. It breaks the newer attempt four ways: invalid metadata, missing source, unsupported schema, and missing profile. In every case the check must fail, and no positive counts may contribute unless the store is flagged invalid.
  - `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` shows that only the latest attempts are selected. Failed and interrupted newest attempts with missing measurements fail the check. After a new build configuration is recorded, only the `build-b` result is selected.
  - `latest_started_retry_replaces_success_and_cannot_be_overwritten_by_old_conversion` shows that a retry replaces the earlier success. A stale update is rejected, and the entry has no measurements until the retry's own are written.
- **No separate report-selection metadata cache.** `a_corrupt_optional_metadata_cache_does_not_hide_saved_measurements` writes a corrupt `selection-cache.json`. It asserts that the store is not invalid and the saved measurements are still selected with the right counts. This probes only one cache file name, but it is a direct and sufficient test of the clause.
- **Identities, states and provenance readable without measurements.** `metadata_queries_skip_measurements_and_snapshots_survive_subsequent_replacement` shows `snapshot(false)` returns tests with `measurements.is_none()`. This holds even after the measurements column is corrupted. `snapshot(true)` still returns them.
- **Only complete, available measurements contribute; pending, running and unavailable entries are reported.** `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[running_and_unreadable_entries_suppress_totals_even_alongside_fresh_measurements]` covers the unavailable (missing profile), pending and running entries.
  - Each case asserts the check fails and the report names the entry, with the outcome text for pending and running.
  - It also asserts that a fresh result is not reported as unavailable and that no totals or line counts appear.
  - Staleness and freshness are cited from `requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. The filtered-runs test also covers them.
- **Checking does not build or execute tests.** `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[book_rendering_preserves_retained_coverage_and_never_launches_tests]` runs `coverage-check` and book rendering with a cargo shim. The shim fails any command other than `metadata`. The test asserts that no forbidden command ran, that the sentinel test did not execute, and that the retained files are unchanged.
- **Replacement and shared artifacts.** `store.rs#fn[focused_replacement_preserves_unselected_results_and_shared_artifacts]` is also marked. It supports the current-set semantics.

No obligation I could derive from the text lacks a test with an assertion, and no {fixme} is needed.

text: :::{req} index.selection
Saved execution-coverage checks read the current coverage set under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.current` from SQLite. Each check
uses one coherent database snapshot of test identities, states, provenance,
and processed measurements, so a replacement or update cannot mix results
from different snapshots within the same check.
Checks do not search historical runs or use a separate report-selection
metadata cache. Current test identities, states, and provenance can be read
without loading their detailed measurements.
Only current results with complete, available measurements contribute to
coverage under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`.
Pending, running, and unavailable entries are reported under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`. Checking does not build
or execute tests and never restores a superseded attempt.
:::{req} storage.current
The coverage set contains at most one current entry for each pair of nextest
binary identity and test name, within one active instrumented build
configuration under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration`.
An entry represents either a test awaiting execution or its current attempt.
Replacing an entry removes its previous measurements from the current set.
Metadata and files shared by remaining current entries stay available. The
store does not accumulate completed historical runs or retry attempts.
:::{req} index.freshness
Only current results whose captured source inputs match the current source
and whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Results with changed
inputs are identified as stale; results of unknown compatibility are
identified as unavailable. Both are excluded from combined totals.
A filtered run preserves the provenance of unselected results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. It does not make those
results fresh when their recorded inputs no longer match. Their process
reports and matching captured source remain available until replacement or
removal of the build artifacts.
:::{req} check.measurement
The coverage check fails when the current store is missing, unreadable, or
corrupt, when no usable coverage has been collected, or when a current entry
is pending, running, missing measurements, unreadable, or stale.
Test execution outcome and measurement availability are distinct. A failed
or interrupted attempt can supply coverage if its measurement processing
completed successfully and its measurements are available. Such an outcome
does not by itself turn its measurements into zero execution or make them
unavailable.
For a current result, every referenced raw profile must remain readable and
nonempty, and matching captured source must remain available. Loss of these
artifacts makes that result's measurements unavailable.
These measurement failures are distinguished from measured lines with zero
execution and from individual functions absent from otherwise usable coverage.
Exception evidence does not excuse measurement failures or permit substitution
of a superseded attempt.
An unsupported store format, or measurements lacking the function attribution
required by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, is rejected
with guidance to recollect coverage. Missing or corrupt metadata that prevents
establishing the current test set, states, provenance, or active configuration
causes failure rather than silently checking the remaining readable records.
